title: Air Quality Alert
location: Lorain; Cuyahoga; Lake; Geauga; Ashtabula Inland; Medina; Summit; Portage; Ashtabula Lakeshore

details.description:
An Air Quality Advisory for ground level fine particles has been
issued by
the Northeast Ohio Areawide Coordinating Agency for Ashtabula,
Cuyahoga, Geauga, Lake, Lorain, Medina, Portage and Summit Counties.

The advisory is from midnight tonight to midnight Thursday night.

A code MAROON air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the local region are extremely hazardous for
the general population. Efforts to minimize effects, even indoors,
may be difficult to impossible. Follow local emergency instructions
via television or radio.

To help our region reduce air pollution:

* Drive less: bike, walk, use transit, work from home, combine trips
* Visit gohiocommute.com/noaca - Find a smarter way to travel!
* Don't idle - Turn off your engine
* Refill your tank after sunset
* Wait to mow the lawn

* At 558 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing

possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result
in debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Steamboat Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the

This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Steamboat Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be
anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in
places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, roads and normally dry arroyos is likely. The heavy rains
will likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep
terrain, especially in and around these areas.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

title: Special Weather Statement
location: Yap Coastal Waters; Chuuk Coastal Waters

details.description:
A broad tropical disturbance, Invest 90W, is slowly organizing
southwest of Pohnpei/southeast of Chuuk near Nukuoro. This
disturbance will remain quasi-stationary for the next 24 to 48 hours
as it slowly develops. Early this weekend, 90W may lift northward
somewhere between Chuuk and Pohnpei.

This disturbance is generating numerous to widespread showers,
isolated thunderstorms and gusty winds across Chuuk and eastern Yap
States. These conditions will shift northward in the coming days.
Sustained winds of 15 to 20 mph, with gusts to 30 mph are possible.

POTENTIAL RAINFALL TOTALS FRIDAY THROUGH MONDAY (JULY 17-20):

Chuuk: 5 to 8 inches
Namoluk: 4 to 7 inches
Losap: 4 to 7 inches
Fananu:5 to 8 inches
Onoun:4 to 7 inches
Polowat: 4 to 7 inches
Pikelot: 3 to 6 inches
Satawal:3 to 6 inches
Olimarao 3 to 6 inches
Gaferut: 3 to 6 inches
Ifalik: 2 to 5 inches
Faraulep: 2 to 5 inches

Locally heavier rainfall is possible depending on the evolution of
Invest 90W in the coming days. Residents across the FSM should keep
up to date with weather forecasts from NWS Guam at
www.weather.gov/gum, and for additional information from both, your
local Weather Service Office and Disaster Coordination Office in
Yap and Chuuk.

For those planning inter-island travel in the next couple of days,
know the weather conditions before you go, and/or consider postponing
travel until conditions improve.

This Special Weather Statement will be updated daily, and more often
when needed.

title: Special Weather Statement
location: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters

details.description:
A broad tropical disturbance, Invest 90W, is slowly organizing
southwest of Pohnpei/southeast of Chuuk near Nukuoro. This
disturbance will remain quasi-stationary for the next 24 to 48 hours
as it slowly develops. Early this weekend, 90W may lift northward
somewhere between Chuuk and Pohnpei.

This disturbance is generating numerous to widespread showers,
isolated thunderstorms and gusty winds across southern Pohnpei and
Kosrae States. These conditions will shift northward in the coming
days. Sustained winds of 15 to 20 mph, with gusts to 30 mph are
possible.

POTENTIAL RAINFALL TOTALS FRIDAY THROUGH MONDAY (JULY 17-20):

Pohnpei: 2 to 4 inches
Kosrae:2 to 4 inches
Mokil:2 to 4 inches
Pingelap:2 to 4 inches
Sapwuafik:3 to 5 inches
Nukuoro: 4 to 6 inches

Locally heavier rainfall is possible depending on the evolution of
Invest 90W in the coming days. Residents across the FSM should keep
up to date with weather forecasts from NWS Guam at
www.weather.gov/gum, and for additional information from both, your
local Weather Service Office and Disaster Coordination Office in
Kosrae and Pohnpei.

For those planning inter-island travel in the next couple of days,
know the weather conditions before you go, and/or consider postponing
travel until conditions improve.

This Special Weather Statement will be updated daily, and more often
when needed.
